questions.html: Refer to the following figure, If $\mathbf{S}_{1}=\mathbf{1}$ and $\mathbf{S}_{2}=\mathbf{0}$ what will be the logic state at the output $\mathbf{X}$ ?
questions.solution:
Answer: Not available

Selected solution (score: 9)

The output $X$ can be written as:

$X = \overline{(\overline{A.\overline{S_1}.\overline{S_2}}) . (\overline{B.\overline{S_1}.S_2}) . (\overline{C.S_1.\overline{S_2}}) . (\overline{D.S_1.S_2})}$

$X = (\overline{\overline{A.\overline{S_1}.\overline{S_2}}}) + (\overline{\overline{B.\overline{S_1}.S_2}}) + (\overline{\overline{C.S_1.\overline{S_2}}}) + (\overline{\overline{D.S_1.S_2}})$

$X = A.\overline{S_1}.\overline{S_2} + B.\overline{S_1}.S_2 + C.S_1.\overline{S_2} + D.S_1.S_2$

It is given in question that $S_1 = 1$ and $S_2 = 0$.

So, only $S_1.\overline{S_2} = 1$ and all other combinations of $S_1$ & $S_2$ will be 0.

Therefore, $X = A.0 + B.0 + C.1 + D.0$

$\implies X = C$ (option C)

Source solution 2 (score: 0)

Table of NAND:

ABO/P
001
011
101
110

From the table of NAND we can observe that NAND gives output 1 when atleast one input is 0. SO we can use this observation.

1st NAND: S1(1) inverts and becomes 0 and gets into NAND so Output of 1st NAND is 1

2nd NAND: S2 0 goes directly into NAND so Output of 2nd NAND is 1

3rd NAND: (s1.s2' . c )' = (1.1.c)' = c'

4th NAND: S2 0 goes directly into NAND so Output of 4th NAND is 1

Final NAND: (1.1.c'.1)' = C 

So, X=C

questions.html: The simplification of the Boolean expression $(\overline{\overline{\boldsymbol{A}} \boldsymbol{B} \overline{\boldsymbol{C}}})+(\overline{\boldsymbol{A} \overline{\boldsymbol{B}} \boldsymbol{C}})$ is
questions.solution:
Answer: B

Selected solution (score: 3)

$ \overline{(\overline{A}B\overline{C})} + \overline{(A\overline{B}C)} = ( \overline{\overline{A}} + \overline{B} + \overline{\overline{C}}  )+ ( \overline{A} +\overline{\overline{B}} + \overline{C}) $

                                $=(\overline{\overline{A}} + {\overline{A}}) + (\overline{\overline{B}} + {\overline{B}}) + (\overline{\overline{C}} + {\overline{C}})$

                                $=(A + {\overline{A}}) + (B + {\overline{B}}) + (C + {\overline{C}})$

                                $=1+1+1$

                                $=1$

Hence, Option B is correct.
